# MM-P2-L1-RR01-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01

Scope
This document defines the method, tools, acceptance criteria, and recordkeeping for inspection and torque verification of structural and rotating assembly fasteners on Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01). It applies to all maintenance and reliability tasks that require removal, replacement, or torque verification of bolt, nut, and stud connections on this machine. The maximum ring outer diameter for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 1125 mm. Follow related procedure guidance in MM-P2-L1-RR01, use safety resources in SB-1013, and follow shop-level routines in SOP-P2-L1-02.

Background and rationale
Proper clamp force on fasteners is essential for maintaining alignment, preventing fretting damage, and avoiding accelerated wear on bearings and mating surfaces. Inspection identifies corrosion, tensile overload, and loss of preload. Torque verification confirms that clamping force is within the range required by the original equipment manufacturer and the engineering drawings referenced in MM-P2-L1-RR01. Where joint condition has changed (galling, deformation, or lubrication change), replacement of hardware and reassembly according to the assembly procedure in MM-P2-L1-RR01 is required.

Tools and consumables
- Calibrated torque wrench suitable for the fastener sizes on EQ-P2-L1-RR01; calibration traceable per plant calibration practice and SB-1013 records.  
- Angle gauge or joint-stretch measurement tool if required by referenced procedures in MM-P2-L1-RR01.  
- Anti-seize, assembly lubricant, or thread lubricant as specified in MM-P2-L1-RR01; lubricant part number for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is CFW-LUB-724.  
- Socket and driver set compatible with fastener heads on EQ-P2-L1-RR01.  
- Torque audit log and inspection checklist form as specified in SOP-P2-L1-02.  
- Clean lint-free rags, solvent for degreasing, and corrosion inhibitor for reassembly as required by MM-P2-L1-RR01.

Procedure
Preparation
- Review the equipment history in MM-P2-L1-RR01 and any recent anomaly reports. Confirm the joint assembly method required for the specific subassembly being serviced. Consult SOP-P2-L1-02 for permits and lockout procedures. Use personal protective equipment per SB-1013 for hot work, pinch points, and lifting.

Initial inspection
- With the area de-energized and the assembly secured, perform a visual inspection of fasteners and mating surfaces. Look for head rounding, thread damage, corrosion, elongation, or evidence of hydrogen embrittlement. Inspect washers and locking devices for distortion or wear. Note any fastener that does not sit flush with its contact surface or that shows asymmetric loading marks.

Cleaning and assessment
- Clean threads and bearing surfaces with a compatible solvent and a lint-free cloth. Remove old lubricant and debris sufficiently to allow accurate torque application and measurement. If threads are damaged beyond assembly tolerance specified in MM-P2-L1-RR01, replace with new hardware per procurement and material control.

Assembly preparation
- Apply the specified lubricant CFW-LUB-724 to threads and bearing faces where the referenced procedure requires lubrication. Use only quantities and application methods defined in MM-P2-L1-RR01; excess or different products can change clamp force characteristics.

Torque verification and application
- Confirm the correct fastener grade and size as required by MM-P2-L1-RR01. Use the calibrated torque wrench and perform a test check outside the assembly to ensure calibration is functioning. For joints where MM-P2-L1-RR01 specifies a direct torque method, apply torque using a smooth, continuous stroke. Where an angle or stretch method is referenced in MM-P2-L1-RR01, use the appropriate measurement tool and follow the sequence required by the engineering notes. For multi-bolt flanges or bearing caps, follow a progressive, opposing sequence to minimize distortion as described in MM-P2-L1-RR01.

Examples and special cases
- Example joint: a loaded bearing cap with matched pairs of bolts. Follow the sequence and method in MM-P2-L1-RR01, clean and relubricate with CFW-LUB-724 before reassembly, then verify clamp force using the method specified in MM-P2-L1-RR01.  
- Example condition: if a fastener shows evidence of yielding or elongation, tag it and replace per MM-P2-L1-RR01. Do not attempt to reuse fasteners that fail visual or mechanical inspection.

Acceptance criteria
- Fasteners must be free of damage, threads must engage fully without cross-threading, and hardware must be the specified grade and condition per MM-P2-L1-RR01.  
- After assembly or verification, all fasteners shall demonstrate clamping performance as required in the engineering documentation referenced in MM-P2-L1-RR01. If nonconformance is detected, or if a fastener shows any sign of deformation or compromised integrity, the component shall be replaced and the joint reassembled following MM-P2-L1-RR01 guidance.  
- Lubrication at assembly must match the lubricant part number CFW-LUB-724 where the referenced procedure indicates a specific thread or seat lubricant.  
- For components that interact with rings, note that the maximum ring outer diameter for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 1125 mm; ensure clearances and guards are restored per MM-P2-L1-RR01 after maintenance.

Records and reporting
- Complete the torque audit log and inspection checklist specified in SOP-P2-L1-02 for every maintenance activity affecting fasteners. Record hardware disposition, lubricant used (record CFW-LUB-724 where applicable), inspection findings, corrective actions, and the identifier of the technician performing the work. Retain records with the maintenance job file and reference MM-P2-L1-RR01 for traceability.  
- If anomalies are found that meet reportable criteria in SB-1013, raise an incident report per SB-1013 and attach inspection documentation.

References
- MM-P2-L1-RR01  
- SB-1013  
- SOP-P2-L1-02

Revision history
- See document control notes in MM-P2-L1-RR01 for revision linkage and superseded procedures.
